event.description: A receiver that does not know an event value ignores the envelope rather than failing. Both Swift ports decode `event` into a closed enum, so an unknown value throws at decode and the transport drops the message -- which is the intended behaviour, not an error to report.

foodLog.description: Present only when event is FOOD_LOGGED (watch -> phone). The envelope's `workoutId` is a fresh one-shot id for this food and `revision` is 1. A phone that has stored the food answers with a WORKOUT_SYNC_ACK carrying the same `workoutId` and `revision`, and stores a `workoutId` it has already stored only once (acknowledging it again). The watch keeps the food in its standalone, exportable log until that acknowledgement arrives, then removes it there, so the food is never in both the phone's log and an export.

plan.description: Present only when event is PLAN_PUSHED (phone -> watch). The envelope's own `workoutId` is the plan's identity and `revision` is the plan's revision, so the existing conflict rule applies unchanged: a receiver ignores a PLAN_PUSHED whose revision it has already seen for that id, and accepts a newer one. PLAN_REQUEST (watch -> phone) carries no `plan` at all; it is a bare envelope asking the phone to push the current one, with a fresh one-shot `workoutId` and revision 1, exactly as FOOD_LOGGED uses those fields.

heartRate.description: Present only when event is SESSION_FINISHED, and only when the watch actually recorded heart rate for that session. Absent means 'not recorded' -- never zero.

plan.description: The workout the watch should run. Ordered: `exercises` is the order to train in, and each exercise's `sets` are the order to perform them in.

source.description: Where the plan came from, so the watch can say so: a routine the lifter saved, or a routine that arrived in a coach's plan link.

scheduledFor.description: The local calendar day this plan is for, as yyyy-MM-dd with no time component -- the same shape PLAN-FORMAT.md uses, and read in the device's own timezone. Absent when the plan is not tied to a date.

equipment.description: Omitted, never empty, when the exercise has none. A lift's identity is name and equipment together.

lastPerformed.description: What the lifter actually did the last time they trained this exercise, so the watch can show 'last: 185x5 @8' beside the prescription. Omitted when there is no history for it.

prescribedSet.description: Every field is optional, keeping PLAN-FORMAT.md's rule that a prescription is often partial: reps with no weight is 'five reps, you pick the weight'. An absent field is absent -- a receiver must never render or store it as zero. A set that prescribes nothing at all is a legal, empty object.

weightKg.description: KILOGRAMS. PLAN-FORMAT.md's set tuple is pounds; this contract is not that format, and both apps store kilograms, so the field name carries the unit rather than leaving it to a convention that can be forgotten. A receiver converts for display only.

restSeconds.description: How long to rest after this set. Absent means the sender has no opinion and the watch uses its own default -- it does not mean zero rest.

lastPerformed.description: An actual, already-performed set. Every field optional for the same reason a prescription's are, plus `performedOn`, the local calendar day it was performed.
